title: Permitted Values for the Continuum: Easton's Converse Direction
description: Formalizes the CONVERSE of the parent König-exclusion file: every regular cardinal κ ≥ ℵ₁ is a PERMITTED value for 2^ℵ₀ (consistent with both Cantor's lower bound and König's cofinality constraint). The pointwise object-level scaffold (IsPermittedValue, aleph_succ_permitted, permitted_unbounded) and the function-level Easton structure (IsEastonFunction, isEastonFunction_continuum) are fully proved from Mathlib. The realizability claim (Easton 1970: every permitted value occurs as 2^ℵ₀ in some forcing extension) is axiomatized at two granularities — pointwise and function-level — pending future formalization of class forcing in Lean.

meta.author: researcher-3
meta.assumptions: 2 axiom declarations (easton_permitted_realizable and easton_consistency) state the realizability direction of Easton's 1970 theorem: every regular κ > ℵ₀ is realizable as 2^ℵ₀, and every Easton function is realizable as the continuum function on regular cardinals. Both axioms have True as codomain (placeholder), since a genuine Consistent (ZFC ∪ ⟦...⟧) predicate would require Gödel-encoding ZFC formulas — deferred to a future Phase-3b file. All 8 supporting theorems are fully machine-checked from Mathlib (axiom-free): IsPermittedValue scaffold, aleph_one_permitted, aleph_two_permitted, aleph_succ_permitted, permitted_satisfies_konig, permitted_unbounded, IsEastonFunction structure, isEastonFunction_continuum, isEastonFunction_nonempty, isEastonFunction_max. S6 (researcher-8) added isEastonFunction_max — closure of the Easton-function class under pointwise binary maximum, using only standard order lemmas (le_max_left, max_le_max, max_eq_left, max_eq_right, le_total).

overview.historicalContext: Easton's 1970 theorem (PhD thesis, Annals of Math. Logic 1) is one of the most striking results in set-theoretic cardinal arithmetic. It completely answers the question 'how arbitrary can the continuum function 2^κ be on regular cardinals?' — by showing that ALL functions F : Reg → Card satisfying three minimal constraints (F(κ) ≥ κ⁺, monotonicity, cf(F(κ)) > κ) are realizable in some forcing extension of ZFC. The constraints are necessary (provable from Mathlib's lt_cof_power and power_le_power_right) but the realizability direction requires class-sized partial orders — Easton product forcing — which extends Cohen's 1963 set-forcing technique to violate GCH simultaneously at every regular cardinal. This file formalizes the converse to OQ-01-OQ-01-OQ-02 (which lists EXCLUDED values): instead of enumerating what 2^ℵ₀ cannot be, it characterizes what 2^ℵ₀ CAN be.
overview.problemStatement: Identify the cardinals consistent with both Cantor's lower bound (2^ℵ₀ > ℵ₀) and König's constraint (cf(2^ℵ₀) > ℵ₀), and formalize Easton's claim that every such 'permitted value' is realizable as 2^ℵ₀ in some forcing extension of ZFC.
overview.proofStrategy: Two-tier approach. (1) PERMITTED VALUES (object-level): Define IsPermittedValue κ := κ.IsRegular ∧ ℵ₀ < κ. Prove from Mathlib that every regular uncountable cardinal satisfies König's constraint, and that successor alephs ℵ_{α+1} are always permitted (giving an inexhaustible supply of permitted values). (2) EASTON FUNCTIONS (function-level): Define IsEastonFunction F as a structure capturing the three constraints succ_le, monotone, konig_pointwise on regular cardinals. Prove that the actual continuum function κ ↦ 2^κ is an Easton function (witness for non-vacuity) using Mathlib's Cardinal.cantor, Cardinal.power_le_power_right, and Cardinal.lt_cof_power. (3) AXIOMATIZE the realizability direction: easton_permitted_realizable (pointwise) and easton_consistency (function-level), with True codomain as placeholder for a future Consistent-of-ZFC predicate.
keyInsights: The two ZFC-provable Easton constraints (Cantor + König) are EXACTLY the binding constraints — there are no further restrictions. This is the deep content of Easton's theorem and what makes the cardinal-arithmetic-on-regulars problem 'almost completely free' (Jech 2003)

Defining IsPermittedValue at the cardinal level (rather than the ordinal level used in OQ-03) gives a more direct converse to the parent file's exclusion theorems: continuum_ne_singular says 'cardinals with cofinality ≤ ℵ₀ are excluded' and aleph_succ_permitted says 'successor alephs are permitted' — these are mirror statements at the same level of abstraction

The Easton function structure on Cardinal → Cardinal (rather than Ordinal → Cardinal) sharpens the OQ-03 ordinal-indexed version: it asks for monotonicity ON REGULAR CARDINALS, not on all ordinals, capturing exactly what Easton's theorem governs

The True codomain on the realizability axioms is the honest framing: a real Consistent predicate would require a Gödel-encoding of ZFC formulas (which Mathlib does not have), so the placeholder cleanly separates 'mathematically what is being claimed' from 'how to express it once the meta-theoretic infrastructure exists'

permitted_unbounded says the permitted values form a proper class — ruling out any 'large cardinal upper bound' interpretation. This is essential: 2^ℵ₀ can be ANY regular uncountable cardinal, including ℵ_{ω₁+1}, ℵ_{(2^ℵ₀)⁺}, etc.

The witness isEastonFunction_continuum (the actual continuum function 2^κ is an Easton function) is more than a sanity check: it confirms that the Easton-function constraint set captures exactly the function-level shadow of forcing-extension behavior, since 2^κ in the ground model already satisfies all three constraints
prerequisites: Cardinal arithmetic: aleph function, cofinality, cardinal exponentiation
Cantor's theorem: κ < 2^κ for all cardinals κ (Mathlib: Cardinal.cantor)
König's theorem: cf(κ^λ) > λ for infinite λ and κ > 1 (Mathlib: Cardinal.lt_cof_power)
Regular cardinals and the Mathlib API: Cardinal.IsRegular, Cardinal.isRegular_aleph_succ, IsRegular.cof_eq
Set-theoretic forcing (for the realizability axioms — not formalized in Lean)

sections.title: Module Header: Permitted-Values Problem and Imports
sections.summary: Documents the converse direction (every regular κ ≥ ℵ₁ is permitted) versus the parent file's exclusion direction (singular cardinals are excluded). Imports Mathlib's Cardinal.Basic, Ordinal, Cofinality, and the parent file Proofs.CantorDiagonalizationOQ01OQ01OQ02 for König-constraint reuse.
sections.mathContext: ZFC's two binding constraints on $2^{\aleph_0}$: $\aleph_0 < 2^{\aleph_0}$ (Cantor) and $\mathrm{cf}(2^{\aleph_0}) > \aleph_0$ (König). The permitted values are exactly the cardinals satisfying both — the regular uncountable cardinals.

sections.title: Permitted Values: Pointwise Characterization
sections.summary: Defines IsPermittedValue κ := κ.IsRegular ∧ ℵ₀ < κ. Proves permitted_satisfies_konig (König), aleph_one_permitted (CH value), aleph_two_permitted (PFA value), aleph_succ_permitted (every successor aleph), and permitted_unbounded (proper class). 6 theorems, 0 axioms, 0 sorries.
sections.mathContext: $\mathsf{IsPermittedValue}(\kappa) \iff \kappa$ is regular and $\aleph_0 < \kappa$. Concretely: $\aleph_1, \aleph_2, \aleph_n, \ldots, \aleph_{\omega+1}, \aleph_{\omega_1+1}, \ldots$ are all permitted. The unbounded-class theorem $\forall \alpha\, \exists \kappa\, (\aleph_\alpha < \kappa \land \mathsf{IsPermittedValue}(\kappa))$ rules out any cardinal upper bound on $2^{\aleph_0}$.

sections.title: Easton Functions: Function-Level Constraints
sections.summary: Defines IsEastonFunction F as a structure with three fields: succ_le (F(κ) ≥ κ⁺), monotone (F monotone on regular cardinals), konig_pointwise (cf(F(κ)) > κ). Proves isEastonFunction_continuum (2^· is Easton), isEastonFunction_nonempty (the constraint set is non-vacuous), and isEastonFunction_max (closure under pointwise binary maximum). 3 theorems, 0 axioms, 0 sorries.
sections.mathContext: The structure $\mathsf{IsEastonFunction}\,F$ captures the function-level Easton conditions on regular cardinals: $F(\kappa) \geq \kappa^+$, $\kappa \leq \lambda \Rightarrow F(\kappa) \leq F(\lambda)$, $\mathrm{cf}(F(\kappa)) > \kappa$. The witness $F(\kappa) = 2^\kappa$ satisfies all three from Mathlib's Cantor, power_le_power_right, and lt_cof_power lemmas. The class is closed under pointwise binary max: $\max(F,G)(\kappa) := \max(F(\kappa), G(\kappa))$ is again Easton, with each constraint preserved by elementary order lemmas.

sections.title: Easton Consistency: Axiomatized Realizability
sections.summary: Axiomatizes Easton's 1970 realizability theorem at two granularities: easton_permitted_realizable (every permitted value κ > ℵ₀ realizable as 2^ℵ₀) and easton_consistency (every Easton function realizable as the continuum function on regulars). Both axioms have True as codomain — a placeholder for a future Consistent-of-ZFC predicate. 2 axiom declarations.
sections.mathContext: $\mathsf{Easton}\,(1970)$: $\mathsf{Con}(\mathsf{ZFC}) \Rightarrow \mathsf{Con}(\mathsf{ZFC} + (\forall \kappa\,\mathrm{regular} \geq \aleph_0:\, 2^\kappa = F(\kappa)))$ for every Easton function $F$. The proof uses Easton product forcing — class-sized partial orders adding $F(\kappa) - \kappa$ many Cohen subsets to $\kappa$ for every regular $\kappa$. Not formalized in Lean.

conclusion.summary: This file establishes the CONVERSE direction to the parent König-exclusion theorem. Object-level: every regular uncountable cardinal is a permitted value of 2^ℵ₀ (9 theorems, 1 def, 0 sorries, 0 axioms in Parts I-II). Meta-level: Easton's 1970 realizability theorem is axiomatized at two granularities (Part III, 2 axioms with True placeholder codomain). Together with the parent file (König exclusion) and OQ-03 sibling (Easton spectrum on aleph indexing), this completes the formalizable picture of the continuum function on regular cardinals modulo class forcing.
conclusion.implications: The cardinal-level (Cardinal → Cardinal) Easton-function structure is a sharper formulation than the aleph-indexed (Ordinal → Cardinal) version in OQ-03: it directly captures the regular-cardinal restriction without requiring auxiliary aleph indexing. This is the right setting for stating the 'continuum function has only Cantor + König constraints' result. Future Phase-3b work can replace the True placeholder with a genuine Consistent predicate — possibly via Gödel-encoded ZFC formulas, possibly via a future Lean port of flypitch's set-forcing infrastructure.
openQuestions: Can a Lean 4 port of flypitch (Han, Van Doorn 2020 — Cohen forcing for CH) be developed and extended to class-sized partial orders for Easton product forcing? This would give the realizability axioms a real proof.

What is the right Lean encoding of 'Consistent (ZFC ∪ {2^ℵ₀ = κ})'? Options: Gödel-encoded formulas with a Provable predicate; or model-existence claim 'there is a structure satisfying ZFC + 2^ℵ₀ = κ'; or a sound-enough fragment of ZFC formalized internally.

Can the singular-cardinal analogue be formalized? Silver's theorem (1975) and Magidor's results show that 2^κ for singular κ is FAR more constrained than for regular κ — this is the Singular Cardinal Hypothesis story, much of which (PCF theory) is provable in ZFC and would not require forcing.

crossReferences.description: The parent file proves König's constraint (cf(2^ℵ₀) > ℵ₀) and enumerates EXCLUDED values for the continuum (singular cardinals, ℵ_ω). This file establishes the CONVERSE: the regular uncountable cardinals are exactly the permitted values, and every permitted value is realizable (axiomatized).

OQ-03 formalizes Easton's spectrum at the ORDINAL-INDEXED level (F : Ordinal → Cardinal, with F(α) ≈ 2^{ℵ_α}). This file uses the CARDINAL-LEVEL formulation (F : Cardinal → Cardinal restricted to regulars), which is closer to the original Easton 1970 statement and gives a more direct converse to the parent's exclusion theorems.
The Cantor-diagonal lower bound κ < 2^κ (used in succ_le for the continuum-function witness) traces back to OQ-01's establishment of the diagonal argument.
Provides the gallery's primary forcing-and-independence narrative; this file slots the 'permitted-values' angle into the broader CH/forcing landscape.
